entries.a_rule: The consumer documentation entry point is the repository root README.md.
entries.b_behavior: The consumer entry point is docs/project.md; checkRegistration roots registration at mdOut.get('project.md').
entries.rationale: The global agent system ships a docs/ tree rooted at project.md rather than a repository README, so registration follows the docs/ entry point.

entries.a_rule: An unlinked note (orphan-note) is an error that fails the run.
entries.b_behavior: checkOrphans pushes orphan-note to warnings, so an unlinked note never fails the run.
entries.rationale: A freshly scaffolded corpus legitimately starts disconnected, so erroring would make bootstrap unusable.

entries.a_rule: Registration is named missing-from-hub and is an error rooted at the root hub.
entries.b_behavior: checkRegistration restores resolver-based registration as the missing-from-entry warning rooted at project.md.
entries.rationale: Registration gaps are advisory while a project is being authored; the name and entry point also changed with the docs/-rooted layout.

entries.a_rule: A near-duplicate document body is reported as a warning.
entries.b_behavior: The check is omitted entirely; the validator header documents the omission in its 'Omitted (documented): near-duplicate-body' note.
entries.rationale: Near-duplicate detection requires a tokenizer and is taste-level, so its cost outweighs the value for this consumer.

entries.a_rule: Tags serialize as '- **tag** — refs' bullet blocks.
entries.b_behavior: renderTagsRegion emits a '## tag' heading per distinct tag with '- `rel` - label' lines.
entries.rationale: The docs/-rooted layout references files by relative path and defines its own generated-region format, covered by the generated-region test.

entries.a_rule: Upstream generates a repository-root index.md rooted at README.md with upstream's own labels and counters.
entries.b_behavior: renderIndexRegion generates a docs/-rooted index.md whose tree is rooted at the entry `project.md` and whose region uses this corpus's serialization (context-doc/note/hub tree labels and its own class counters).
entries.rationale: The consumer docs/ corpus has no repository README; it is rooted at project.md, so index.md serializes that entry point and this corpus's class vocabulary instead of upstream's README-rooted shape.
entries.test: tmp=$(mktemp -d) && cp -r tests/fixtures/docs-corpus/valid/. "$tmp/" && node templates/docs-validate.js --root "$tmp" --write >/dev/null 2>&1 && grep -q "### Tree" "$tmp/index.md" && rm -rf "$tmp"

entries.a_rule: Findings are printed without a severity prefix.
entries.b_behavior: Findings are prefixed with 'error:'/'warning:' and carry a real path:line location.
entries.rationale: Severity prefixes make findings machine-filterable and path:line lets an editor jump to the offending line.

entries.a_rule: Upstream sorts all findings by path:line before printing.
entries.b_behavior: main prints every warning first, then every error, each group in check order instead of a merged path:line sort.
entries.rationale: Reporting the advisory warnings and the failing errors as separate groups keeps the summary counters legible and the exit status unambiguous.
entries.test: node templates/docs-validate.js --root tests/fixtures/docs-corpus/invalid | grep -nE "^(warning|error):" | head -1 | grep -q "^[0-9]*:warning:"

entries.a_rule: The summary line reports the counts and files scanned without the corpus root.
entries.b_behavior: main appends `(root: <dir>)` to the summary line so the scanned corpus is identifiable.
entries.rationale: The validator can be pointed at any corpus with --root, so echoing the resolved root makes results self-describing in CI logs.

entries.a_rule: Upstream walks the corpus skipping only its own infrastructure directories.
entries.b_behavior: collect additionally skips node_modules and .agent-backups via SKIP_DIRS.
entries.rationale: A consumer project's docs/ sits inside a code repo, so node_modules and the agent system's .agent-backups snapshots must never be scanned.

entries.a_rule: A non-kebab folder is reported at the folder path.
entries.b_behavior: checkNames reports each offending folder at the offending file path (d.rel) that sits inside it.
entries.rationale: Findings are emitted as path:line, so attributing the folder violation to a concrete scanned file keeps the location editor-jumpable.
